$comment: Generated by build/Update-ReviewChecklist.ps1 from each guide's Checklist section, in sidebar order; do not edit.

groups.title: Derive a key from a password
items: The derived key is in a buffer from `Rent(..., isSensitive: true, ...)`, or in stack memory under `GetSecureLifetime()`, never in a returned `byte[]`.
The owner of that buffer is in a `using`.
No `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(password)`.
Algorithm objects that took the key, such as `AesGcm`, are disposed in the same scope.
Nothing derived is logged, encoded as text or copied with `ToArray()`.
A derived value is compared with `FixedTimeEquals`.

groups.title: Verify a MAC without leaking timing
items: The comparison is `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`, never `==`, `Equals`, `SequenceEqual` or `StartsWith`.
The incoming value is decoded to bytes; the expected value is never encoded as text.
The expected value is under `GetSecureLifetime()`, or another owner that zeroes it.
A value of the wrong length is rejected before it is decoded.
The MAC key is held in a buffer that is zeroed when its owner is disposed.

groups.title: Work with an API that takes or returns byte[]
items: A `byte[]` that holds a secret comes from `CreatePinnedArray`, in a `using`.
An array an API returned is wrapped with `GetSecureLifetime()` on the next line.
The span overload is used wherever one exists.
No lifetime or key array reaches a logger, a field or a lambda.
No method returns the array from inside its `using` scope.
Algorithm objects that took a key are disposed.

groups.title: Turn a secret between text, Base64, hex and bytes
items: Every key and password is made with `RentDecoded`, `RentBytes`, `RentChars`, `RentEncoded` or `RentRandom`, and not with `Convert.FromBase64String`, `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes` or `RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes`.
Every call that handles a secret passes `isSensitive: true`; a nonce, which is not secret, may pass `false`.
The owner is held in the scope that uses its span, and disposed with `using`.
`FormatException` and `EncoderFallbackException` are caught where the input enters.
JOSE values, such as a JWK's key or a JWS signature, are decoded with `Base64UrlStrict`, not `Base64Url`.
Nothing copies the span with `ToArray()` or `new string(…)`.

groups.title: Build a secret of unknown length, and read it as one span
items: The secret is written into `CreatePooledBufferWriter(isSensitive: true)`, in a `using`.
No `MemoryStream`, `ArrayBufferWriter<T>`, `List<byte>` or `StringBuilder` holds it.
Secret values enter the JSON writer as bytes, never as a `string`.
An API that takes pieces is fed the segments.
A lease or a consumed owner is sensitive, and in a `using`.
No `ToArray()` on the writer, its sequence or a lease.

groups.title: Build a secret that grows, in one piece
items: A secret that grows is written into `CreateContiguousBufferWriter`, `CreatePooledStream` or `PooledTextBuilder`, and not into an `ArrayBufferWriter<byte>`, a `MemoryStream` or a `StringBuilder`.
A secret passes `isSensitive: true`; data that is not secret may pass `false`.
The writer, stream or builder is disposed with `using`.
Nothing keeps a span across the next `GetSpan` or `GetMemory`.
The text builder is passed by `ref` and is never copied, never held in a field, and never kept across an `await`.
Nothing calls `ToString()` on a builder that holds a secret.

groups.title: Read a secret without leaving a string behind
items: No `GetString`, `ReadAllText` or deserialized `string` property holds a secret.
Values are copied or decoded straight into a buffer from `Rent(…, isSensitive: true, …)`.
Each buffer is sized with an upper bound and sliced to the count written, or comes from `RentDecoded`, `RentBytes` or `RentChars`, which size it for you.
`DecoderFallbackException` is caught at the boundary, and never logged.
Every owner is in a `using`.

groups.title: Keep a secret in a field without printing it
items: A secret that lives in a field or crosses an `await` is a `Secret<T>`, and not a `string` or a `byte[]`.
Every read goes through `Reveal()`, so a search for `Reveal` finds them all.
Nothing copies the revealed value to an array or a `string`.
Comparisons use `FixedTimeEquals`, and nobody uses `Equals` or `GetHashCode()` on a secret where the length matters.
A key that does not exist yet is created with `Secret.Create<T, TState>`, so it is written straight into the secret.
The secret is disposed, and no thread disposes it while another reads it.

groups.title: Keep a secret across an await, or in a field
items: Async code rents with `out Memory<byte>`.
A long-lived key is in an `IMemoryOwner<byte>` held by a disposable class, never in a `byte[]` field.
The holder is disposed at shutdown or rotation, once nothing uses it.
No view of the buffer outlives its owner.
Span work is in synchronous helpers, or in blocks that end before the next `await`.

groups.title: Give pipes and stream readers a pool that cleans up
items: Every `new Pipe(` and every `PipeReader.Create(` that carries a secret is given a pool of `SecureMemoryPool<byte>`.
The pool is owned by the application, and disposed once, at shutdown.
The minimum segment size is 4096 bytes or less.
Both ends of the pipe are completed on every path.
Nothing copies the pipe's bytes into an ordinary array.
A read that an API wants as one span is read with `GetSpanLease(isSensitive: true)`, and the lease is disposed.

groups.title: Reject malformed UTF-8 and ASCII
items: Every decode of bytes you did not write uses `SecureEncoding.UTF8` or `SecureEncoding.ASCII`, never `Encoding.UTF8` or `Encoding.ASCII`.
A `DecoderFallbackException` is caught where the input enters, and turned into a rejection.
The rejection does not decode the bytes again with another encoding.
A `StreamReader` is given the encoding and `detectEncodingFromByteOrderMarks: false`.
Nothing logs the exception or its `BytesUnknown`.

groups.title: Serialize into a buffer that must not grow
items: The buffer is sized for the largest output, and for the largest request the serializer makes.
A helper takes the writer by `ref`, never by value.
`Advance` is called with the number of bytes written, never `span.Length`.
A partial write is followed by `Reset()` where the failure is caught.
A buffer that holds a secret is a sensitive rental or is under a lifetime, so that something zeroes all of it.

groups.title: Split delimited text without copying substrings
items: Pieces are read as spans or `ReadOnlyMemory<char>`, and no piece is turned into a string with `ToString()`.
Names are compared with `StringComparison.Ordinal`, on spans.
A piece that outlives the original is copied into a buffer that something zeroes.
`First` is read only after `IsEmpty` is checked, and a hot loop walks `First` and `Next` instead of using `foreach`.
Text that holds a secret is split in a sensitive buffer, never in a `string`.
